sentences.text: Psephosauriscus was an extinct genus of placodont reptile that lived during the Middle Triassic in Israel and Egypt.

The animal is known from bony armor plates found at Makhtesh Ramon in the Negev desert and Araif en Naqua on the Sinai Peninsula, where such armor is abundant in Middle Triassic limestone comparable to the Muschelkalk of Europe.
The type species P. mosis is known from a single specimen containing portions of the carapace and plastron.
The scutes covering the armor plates have less defined shapes than the hexagonal osteoderms beneath them, and some osteoderms possess a raised keel.
P. cf. rhombifer is distinguished from other species by the rectangular shape of its scutes.
The carapace osteoderms of P. ramonensis have smoother edges and lack the keel found in species like P. mosis.
Swedish paleontologist F. Brotzen described armor from Makhtesh Ramon in 1957, naming the species Psephosaurus mosis and Psephosaurus picardi.
Austrian paleontologist Georg Haas named the species P. sinaiticus and P. rhombifer in 1959.
Rieppel tentatively described P. cf. rhombifer based on additional material from Araif en Naqua that showed similarities to other Psephosauriscus species.
The genus belongs to the parent group Cyamodontoidea.
The animal is classified in the class Reptilia.
Fossils come from the Beneckeia beds of the Anisian stage and the Ceratites beds spanning the end of the Anisian and beginning of the Ladinian stages.
It is debated whether P. rhombifer belongs to Psephosauriscus because the original holotype specimen described by Haas was lost.
